en.title: Holy, Holy, Holy! Lord God Almighty!
en.author: Reginald Heber
stanzas:
[D]Holy, [Bm]holy, [A7]ho[D]ly! [G]Lord God Al[D]mighty!
[A]Early [D]in [A]the [Bm]morning our song shall [E7]rise to [A]Thee;
[D]Holy, [Bm]holy, [A7]ho[D]ly, [G]merciful and [D]mighty!
[Bm]God in [D7]three [G]Persons, [D]blessèd [A7]Trini[D]ty!

Holy, holy, holy! All the saints adore Thee,
Casting down their golden crowns around the glassy sea;
Cherubim and seraphim falling down before Thee,
Who was, and is, and evermore shall be.

Holy, holy, holy! though the darkness hide Thee,
Though the eye of sinful man Thy glory may not see;
Only Thou art holy; there is none beside Thee,
Perfect in power, in love, and purity.

Holy, holy, holy! Lord God Almighty!
All Thy works shall praise Thy name, in earth, and sky, and sea;
Holy, holy, holy; merciful and mighty!
God in three Persons, blessèd Trinity!

notes: Text: Cyber Hymnal (Heber 1826), which prints each stanza on five typographic lines; reflowed here to the four metrical lines of 11.12.12.10, no words changed. Hymnary's representative text (Hymns and Devotions for Daily Worship #184a) agrees word for word apart from lowercased pronouns and "pow'r" for "power", and capitalises "Holy, Holy, Holy" inconsistently in stanza 3 -- which is why the Cyber Hymnal form was preferred. "blessèd" keeps the source's grave accent (sung as two syllables). Key: hymnary's incipit database lists NICAEA in E major, but Trinity Hymnal p.100 and the Hymn Fake Book both print it in D, so D was taken as the common hymnal key -- already a guitar key, no transposition needed. Chords are a simplification of the Trinity-keyed chart at hymnchords.net. SCANSION: only stanza 1's second line is the 12 syllables the meter names; stanzas 2-4 have 13 there ("Casting down their golden crowns around the glassy sea"), which the tune absorbs on a repeated note. Hymnary's instance list shows several hymnals giving up and calling the meter Irregular for this reason; 11.12.12.10 is what the text authority page states and is used here.
